cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, is in the fourteenth year of his reign. Then Sennacherib, king of Assyria, attacks the fortified cities of Judah. Walls, gates, guards, the whole deal.

cards.question: Sennacherib king of Assyria goes after Judah's fortified cities. How many of them does he capture?

cards.text: ALL of them. Then the king of Assyria sends the Rabshakeh, a royal officer, out from Lachish with a great army.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh marches out of Lachish with a great army. Who is the king of Assyria sending him to?

cards.text: He stops by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field. Three of Hezekiah's men go out to meet him: Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh tells the three men to carry a message to Hezekiah. Whose words does he say he's bringing?

cards.text: And the first question is, "What is the basis of this confidence of yours?" That's a man standing in YOUR driveway asking what makes you think you can park there.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh says Hezekiah's claim to have a strategy and strength for war is nothing but ___ words.
Then the Rabshakeh asks, "In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?" Which nation does he say Judah is leaning on?
The Rabshakeh has a picture for what it's like to lean on Egypt. What does he call Egypt?

answers.text: A splintered reed of a staff
A crumbling wall with no gate
A dry well with no water

cards.text: That reed, he says, will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it, and Pharaoh is the same to all who trust in him. Then he guesses what they might say back, "We trust in the LORD our God," and he has a reply ready.

cards.question: In his reply, the Rabshakeh says Hezekiah has removed the LORD's high places and altars.

cards.text: Then he says, "Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria." Friend, when the man parked outside your city with a great army says let's make a deal, hold on TIGHT to your cookie box.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh offers Hezekiah two thousand horses. What's the catch?

answers.text: If they can put riders on them
If they pay silver for each one
If they open the city gates first

cards.text: That's handing a man the keys to a whole fleet of cars and asking, "Oh, you don't have drivers?" Then he says they can't push back even one of his master's least officers while they depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh claims someone told him, "Go up against this land and destroy it." Who does he say it was?

cards.text: Eliakim, Shebna and Joah cut in: "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it." Not in Hebrew, they tell him.

cards.question: The three officials ask the Rabshakeh not to speak Hebrew in the hearing of whom?
The Rabshakeh agrees to switch to Aramaic for the three officials.

cards.text: Not a chance. He says his master sent these words for the men sitting on the wall too, men he says are destined to eat their own dung and drink their own urine.
The officials asked him to keep it quiet. So the Rabshakeh stands up and goes right over their heads. LITERALLY. Up to the wall.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh now calls out loudly in Hebrew so the people on the wall can hear.

cards.text: "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!" And the king's words are, "Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you."

cards.question: According to the Rabshakeh, what is Hezekiah persuading the people to trust in?

cards.text: Hezekiah's been saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria." So the Rabshakeh switches from threats to a sales pitch: make peace with me and come out to me.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh says if the people make peace and come out, what will every one of them get?

answers.text: To eat from his own vine and fig tree
A place in the king of Assyria's army
A bag of silver from the king's treasury

cards.question: The Rabshakeh promises the people they can stay in their own land for good.

cards.text: They get all that until he comes and takes them away to a land like their own, a land of grain and new wine. That's the free trial, friend, and page nine of the fine print says WE'RE MOVING YOU.

Then he asks, "Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?" He names the gods of Hamath, Arpad and Sepharvaim, and asks whether they delivered Samaria from his hand.

cards.question: After naming all those gods, what does the Rabshakeh ask about the LORD?

answers.text: How He can deliver Jerusalem from Assyria
Why He would ever send Egypt to help
When He will finally send them a sign

cards.text: That's the whole speech. Now everybody on that wall has heard it, and it's their turn to answer.

cards.question: After everything the Rabshakeh shouts at them, how do the people on the wall respond?
The people say nothing, because Hezekiah had commanded, "Do not ___ him."

cards.text: Not one word, friend, and I spent enough years in a junk drawer to know a LOUD silence when I hear one. Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah head back to King Hezekiah.

cards.question: When Eliakim, Shebna and Joah come back to King Hezekiah, what's different about them?

cards.text: They relay the Rabshakeh's words to Hezekiah. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because trust me, this story is NOT done.
